context.text: Blake prefers working on genuinely hard problems where he can have direct impact. He values roles that combine architecture, client strategy, and hands-on engineering. He has experience leading cross-functional teams and internal enablement initiatives.

Blake has deep expertise with Cloudflare's edge platform including Workers, D1, Durable Objects, Workflows, KV, R2, and Queues. He builds production applications on this stack and understands the nuances of edge computing patterns, real-time systems, and serverless architecture at scale.

Blake builds agent infrastructure across four layers. The harness: Felix, a managed-agents harness on Cloudflare Workers where manifest-defined agents compile into runtimes exposed over OpenAI-compatible chat, A2A, MCP, and REST/SSE, with swappable session strategies, seven orchestration patterns (ReAct, deep planning, router, parallel fan-out, group-chat, reflect, plan-execute), transport-labelled tool executors, HITL approvals, evals, and an agentic commerce layer (ACP, Stripe, B2B). The evaluation layer: Memoturn, an open-source AI engineering platform for building, evaluating, and monitoring LLM applications in production: OpenTelemetry tracing, offline and online evals with human review, a versioned prompt registry with deployment channels, and cost/token/latency analytics. The governance layer: Fold, an enterprise MCP gateway in Go that federates every MCP server behind one governed endpoint with deny-by-default policy, OAuth token exchange, and credential brokering so agents never hold raw API keys. The skills layer: Skillist, a realtime agent-skills registry on Cloudflare Workers where agents publish, version, improve, and discover reusable skills, following the agentskills.io spec. All four are his own work, built outside client engagements, and all four are active in 2026: Felix at docs.felix.run, Memoturn at memoturn.com, Fold at fold.run, Skillist at skillist.io. Earlier iterations ran on AWS Bedrock and AgentCore with LangGraph behind a FastAPI gateway. For his agentic work at Adobe, see the adobe-agentic context. Hands-on with LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith, and Claude; he understands prompt engineering, vector search, durable agent memory, human-in-the-loop workflows, and protocol-based agent interop.

Blake's current work at Adobe is the agentic layer for enterprise customer experience, on top of the Adobe Commerce and AEM Edge Delivery Services stack he has been shipping for Fortune 500 clients since 2022. Two products anchor it. Adobe Experience Platform Agent Orchestrator is the orchestration layer behind Experience Platform Agents: it plans the work a request implies, calls the specialized agents needed to do it, and returns a single unified response, with human oversight throughout. CX Enterprise Coworker is Adobe's agentic customer experience platform, announced at Adobe Summit in April 2026 and generally available in June 2026. Given a goal and parameters it takes multiple actions on its own, acting as an AI teammate inside planning, production, and workflow tools across the customer lifecycle. It coordinates agents and workflows across analytics, content creation, and journey orchestration, and synthesizes context from both Adobe and third-party applications, with governance and human approval built in. Blake works on both sides of these products: he builds client solutions with them for Fortune 500 deployments, and he has contributed to their core code. If someone asks what Blake is working on now, or about agentic AI at Adobe, this is the answer.

Blake has led production implementations for Fortune 500 companies at Adobe. He knows how large systems fail and how to migrate them without breaking things. He has experience with zero-downtime migrations, governance frameworks, and architectural review processes.
